history.summary: Temple structure dated to the 13th century CE under the Ganga kings; Kalinga Nagara style (Rekha Deula with Jagamohana). Tradition holds that the black-stone Gopinath deity was carved by Rama at Chitrakut and brought to Remuna by King Langula Narasimha Deva (Langula Narasingha Dev) in the 13th century. About 500 years ago the deity 'stole' Khira (condensed-milk sweet, Amrita Keli/Amruta Keli) for the saint Madhavendra Puri, giving the name Khirachora ('kheer thief'); Madhavendra Puri also instituted the first Chandan Yatra here. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu visited en route to Puri. Recognised as a State Protected Monument (Odisha State Archaeology).

name: Khirachora Gopinath Temple
town_description: Remuna (also spelled Ramuna) is a small town about 9 km east of Balasore on the eastern coast of Odisha; its name derives from 'Ramaniya' (beautiful). Known as Gupt Vrindavana, it is a major Vaishnavite pilgrimage centre famous for the Khirachora Gopinath Temple and its Amrita Keli kheer prasad. It lies roughly midway between Howrah and Bhubaneswar on the east-coast rail corridor.

travel.railway: Balasore railway station (~9 km); then taxi/bus/auto to Remuna
travel.road: Remuna is ~9 km east of Balasore on Mandir Road; small walk from the Remuna bus/taxi stop to the temple
